properties.areaDesc: Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 31 at 9:36PM EDT until November 1 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 7
feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Saint Lucie and Coastal Martin Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 PM EDT Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...Some flooding of low-lying lots, parks and roadways
may occur near the shoreline. Only isolated road closures are
expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 31 at 3:28PM HST until November 2 at 6:00PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
...HIGH SURF ADVISORY FOR NORTH AND WEST FACING SHORES OF NIIHAU
KAUAI AND OAHU...
...HIGH SURF ADVISORY FOR NORTH FACING SHORES OF MOLOKAI AND
MAUI...

.A moderate, long-period northwest (330 degrees) swell is expected
to arrive this evening, and quickly build overnight. Advisory
level surf is expected to Sunday for north and west facing
shores exposed to the swell, with the swell expected to continue
into Monday. The swell may shift to a slightly more northerly
direction for a brief time Monday, before declining Tuesday.

* WHAT...For north facing shores, building to 15 to 20 feet. For
west facing shores, building to 10 to 14 feet.

* WHERE...North and west facing shores of Niihau, Kauai and Oahu,
and north facing shores of Molokai and Maui.

* WHEN...From 6 AM Sunday to 6 PM HST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate. Strong breaking waves and strong currents
will make swimming dangerous.
properties.instruction:
Heed all advice from ocean safety officials. When in doubt, don't
go out.

COLORADO AVALANCHE INFORMATION CENTER.

...A SPECIAL AVALANCHE ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM 4:30 PM SATURDAY
UNTIL 4:30 PM MONDAY...

*WHAT...Avalanche conditions are dangerous above treeline.
*WHERE...West Elk Mountains, Elk Mountains, San Juan Mountains, and
La Plata Mountains
*WHEN...From 4:30 PM Saturday until 4:30 PM Monday.

avalanches large enough to bury a human.

avalanche danger Sunday into Monday. Rain, snow, and wind will cause
natural avalanches above treeline. Check the forecast at
www.colorado.gov/avalanche.

Beyer & Pritchett

properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued October 31 at 5:57PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
Scattered showers will continue across the coastal waters through
late tonight. With increasing instability and enhanced potential
for rotating storms, isolated waterspouts will be possible
tonight, mainly from the coastal waters off Central Coast
southward to the inner waters south of Point Conception. These
same areas will also have a 5-10 percent chance of thunderstorms.

Waterspouts are dangerous and can capsize boats. Never move
closer to investigate or take photos. The best way to avoid a
waterspout is to move at a 90 degree angle to its apparent
movement.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 31 at 8:42PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity for the
following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent east-northeast winds and downstream tidal effects on the
St John River have slowed flow at Astor. Forecast rainfall may lead
to additional rises within Moderate flood stage.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EDT Saturday the stage was 3.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EDT Saturday was 3.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 3.7 feet
Monday evening.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday afternoon at noon EST.

properties.areaDesc: Kauai, HI
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 31 at 2:19PM HST until October 31 at 5:45PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
FFWHFO

The National Weather Service in Honolulu has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The island of Kauai in Kauai County

* Until 545 PM HST.

* At 219 PM HST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain falling over the eastern slopes of Kauai with additional
showers moving in from the southwest. Rain was falling at a rate of
up to 1 to 2 inches per hour. In addition to the Hanalei River, a
rapid rise was also observed along the South Fork of the Wailua
River. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly,
especially near the Hanalei Bridge on the Kuhio Highway and near
the mouth of the Wailua River. Kuhio Highway remains closed near
the Hanalei Bridge.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
The entire island of Kauai.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.
